headline: Placed noise ordinance review and Hospital Guard item on file; approved June 23 minutes.
summary: Councilors discussed the city's noise ordinance with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services and the Police Chief. Chairman's Orders asked for a draft ordinance raising noise fines, a review of public hearings for one-day event licenses, and a report on License Commission steps. The Hospital Guard item and its police staffing discussion were also placed on file.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 23, 2026 Public Safety Committee meeting.
Moved to recommend placing the noise ordinance review item (# 13b CC July 21, 2026) on file.
Moved to recommend placing the Hospital Guard communication item (# 7a CC June 2, 2026) on file.

. Miscellaneous Item 3 
September 8, 2026 Page 2 of 8Public Safety Committee
Order of Councilor Tony Economou, Councilor Jose A. Rivera, Councilor Kathleen M . 
Toomey, Councilor Gary Rosen and Councilor Robert A. Bilotta - Request Standing 
Committee on Public Safety hold a discussion to review the city’s ordinance relative to 
excessive and unreasonable noise. Further, request said discussion include the feasibility 
of amending the noise ordinance to allow for the creation of a special noise variance 
application for churches, festivals, or organizations holding certain events (see attached 
for Worcester noise ordinance, as well as other municipalities’ processes).
# 13b CC July 21, 2026
a.
September 8, 2026 Page 3 of 8Public Safety Committee
Chairperson Councilor Toomey read the item and recognized the Commissioner of Inspectional 
Services, who provided an overview of the city’s noise ordinance, which included enforcement 
roles between the Worcester Police Department (WPD) and the Inspectional Services Department 
(ISD), as well as best methods used to approach noise complaints at establishments. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey discussed problem properties and the feasibility of establishing a 
chronic ambient noise policy with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the process used 
by the License Commission to grant one -day and yearly entertainment licenses to establishments , 
permissible event operation hours relative to religious buildings, permitted operations under a 
one-day event license, the request within the one -day event license application for additional 
amplification permitting, and the process relative to enforcing one -day event license violations 
with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey discussed ISD investigating reported noise complaints within 
standard business hours with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed rules within 
event licenses that exempt certain noise ordinance guidelines, late night reports of excessive noise 
being triaged by WPD, the process relative to inform the License Commission of repeated event 
violations at an establishment, and issues relative to event parking with the Commissioner of 
Inspectional Services and Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager request City Solicitor provide City Council with a draft ordinance amending the city’s 
noise ordinance by increasing fines associated with violations of excessive noise.”
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the feasibility of 
requiring WPD officers to be present at permitted events with the Commissioner of Inspectional 
Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the process relative 
to notify abutters of locations with approved one -day event licenses and an increase in one -day 
event applications with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey brought forth the following two (2) Chairman’s Orders: “1) 
Request City Manager review the feasibility of requiring that public hearings take place before the 
License Commission for all one -day event license applications, with public notices being sent to all 
abutters in the vicinity of the proposed location; and 2) Request City Manager request 
Commissioner of Inspectional Services ensure data is provided at all one -day event license 
hearings before the License Commission that identifies whether the property has received 
complaints and /or citations relative to excessive noise and event permits for the purpose of 
increasing noise ordinance enforcement.”
Chairperson Councilor Toomey discussed event capacity limits with the Commissioner of 
Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the process 
related for ISD to inform WPD of weekly events occurring in the city with the Commissioner of 
September 8, 2026 Page 4 of 8Public Safety Committee
Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey discussed required training to measure and analyze noise and the 
feasibility of staffing ISD personnel at permitted events to measure excessive noise in lieu of a 
WPD officer with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Bergman, who highlighted the importance 
of neighborhood testimony relative to issuing event licenses and issues relating to the early meeting 
times of the License Commission with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey then discussed issues relative to unlicensed events occurring in the 
city and the process relative to revoking an establishment’s Certificate of Occupancy due to 
hosting unlicensed events with the Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed referring to the 
building code to enforce repeated event violations with higher monetary penalties with the 
Commissioner of Inspectional Services. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager request Commissioner of Inspectional Services provide City Council with a report 
detailing the step -by-step process used by the License Commission to approve event license 
applications. Said report should also include the requirement for public hearings, the process used 
to notify event location abutters, a list of identified problem properties, and best practices used in 
other communities relative to event permitting and permit violation enforcement.”
Chairperson Councilor Toomey moved to recommend the item be placed on file.

. Communication of the City Manager - Police Department 4 
September 8, 2026 Page 6 of 8Public Safety Committee
Transmitting informational communication relative to the Hospital Guard of the 
Worcester Police Department.
# 7a CC June 2, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Toomey read the item and recognized the Police Chief, who provided an 
overview related to the role of Hospital Guard of the Worcester Police Department (WPD) and 
discussed challenges relative to staffing capacity within the department.
Chairperson Councilor Toomey discussed the feasibility of establishing a secured unit within the 
hospitals to reduce the need of individual Hospital Guards per detainee and contract negotiations 
to mitigate staffing challenges with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the process 
relative to staffing hospital transportation for detainees and the effect said arrangements have on 
patrol/route officer staffing with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the need for 
additional police officers within the department and the feasibility of staffing two (2) officer patrol 
cars with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed short -term 
methods to institute a two (2) officer patrol car practice with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager provide City Council with a report detailing the feasibility of increasing the Worcester 
Police Department (WPD) personnel to ensure the staffing of two (2) officers per route /patrol car . 
Said request report should also include an estimated cost analysis to institute such a practice.”
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Bergman, who discussed the feasibility of 
establishing precinct police stations to mitigate officer travel times with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager provide City Council with an update concerning a previously adopted order from July 
21, 2026, which read, ‘Request City Manager request Police Chief provide City Council with a 
report detailing incentives and efforts provided by other cities and towns relative to recruiting 
lateral police transfers.’”
Chairperson Councilor Toomey recognized Councilor Economou, who discussed the feasibility of 
working with the Worcester County Sheriff’s Office as a method of mitigating temporary staffing 
challenges with the Police Chief. 
Chairperson Councilor Toomey moved to recommend the item be placed on file. 
Recommend File
